headline: NATO jets scramble in Poland and Romania as Russia hits Ukraine; EU unlocks €4.2bn for Hungary; DJI Bluetooth CVE hits 16 drone models; German entry-level IT jobs down ~77% since 2022.

stories.title: NATO jets scramble in Poland and Romania as Russia strikes Ukraine
facts: ABC News: overnight Russia launched 161 drones (82 jet-powered) plus Banderol cruise missiles into Ukraine; air defenses intercepted/suppressed 119 drones and three cruise missiles; impacts at 18 locations.
Poland’s Armed Forces Operational Command: fighters scrambled “to ensure safety” over jet-powered UAV strikes on western Ukraine; alert ~1 hour; no Polish airspace violation recorded.

Romania MoD / AGERPRES: two F-16s from Borcea scrambled after radar tracked a target NE of Vylkove (Ukraine) near the border; RO-Alert to northern Tulcea; later “no incursions into national airspace.”
Kyiv mayor Klitschko: 1 killed and 7 injured in the capital overnight; SES also reported injuries in Zaporizhzhia, Zhytomyr, and Kharkiv regions.
stories.whyItMatters: Allied air policing along NATO’s eastern flank remains on a hair-trigger as Russia’s overnight drone/missile waves brush the Polish and Romanian borders.

image.alt: Aftermath imagery tied to overnight Russian strikes on Ukraine

stories.title: EU unlocks €4.2bn for Hungary and reopens Erasmus+ / Horizon
facts: Euronews: Commission proposes unlocking €4.2bn in previously frozen cohesion funds after judging Budapest met rule-of-law conditions; also reopens Erasmus+ and Horizon Europe to Hungarian students/researchers.
Funds were suspended in 2022 (~€6.3bn under the conditionality mechanism) over anti-corruption, conflicts of interest, and procurement under Orbán.
Von der Leyen: “Hungary has taken important steps to strengthen the rule of law… Today, we are proposing to unlock €4.2 billion.”

May deal with PM Péter Magyar envisioned up to €16.4bn contingent on 27 “super milestones”; ~€2bn cohesion still blocked (asylum, child protection, academic freedom); €10bn recovery-fund request still under assessment.
stories.whyItMatters: Brussels is cashing in Magyar’s post-Orbán reform checklist — a rare unfreeze that also reopens EU research and exchange programmes to Hungary.

image.alt: Ursula von der Leyen and Péter Magyar at EU headquarters

stories.title: CVE-2026-78306: unauthenticated DJI Bluetooth DUML on 16 drone models
facts: CVE-2026-78306 (CIRCL): unauthenticated DUML over Bluetooth — in-range attacker can change Wi-Fi SSID/PSK/MAC/country/channel, disable/restart radios, disconnect clients, or reset wireless config.
Overwrite Wi-Fi PSK → join the drone’s internal Wi-Fi and potentially reach flight-control interfaces; DoS can cut operator control/video/telemetry mid-flight.
Affected (until fixed firmware): Neo, Neo 2, Flip, Air 3/3S, Avata 2/360, Mavic 3 / Classic / Pro / 4 Pro, Mini 2 / 3 / 3 Pro / 4 Pro / 5 Pro — remediation is a vendor firmware update.
Golem.de amplifies the advisory for German readers today; mid-air full takeover was not demonstrated as a completed PoC in the public summaries.
stories.whyItMatters: Consumer DJI fleets that skip firmware updates can be disrupted — or worse — by anyone close enough for Bluetooth.

stories.title: German entry-level job postings down ~⅔ since 2022 — IT −77%
facts: Tagesschau/Indeed: entry-level job ads since the 2022 peak are down about two-thirds; overall ads fell ~39% — newcomers hit harder than the market.
heise: IT applications/solutions −77% (steepest of 28 groups); marketing −75%; project management −60%; only care/pharma (+18%) and food/hospitality (+10%) rose.
Indeed economist Virginia Sondergeld: risk of a cohort starting with unemployment; decline began summer 2022 — “before ChatGPT” — so a clean AI-displacement signal isn’t in the data yet.
Apprenticeships (incl. dual study) look more resilient than graduate entry roles; Eurostat youth unemployment 2025 ~7.1%.
stories.whyItMatters: Germany’s soft economy is rationing junior seats first — especially in knowledge/IT roles — even while apprenticeships hold up better.

image.alt: Tagesschau coverage of shrinking entry-level job offers

stories.title: DRAM die value now tops leading-edge logic on a $/mm² basis
facts: Tom’s Hardware (Anton Shilov, Sep 22): Kurnal Insights estimates 1b DRAM at ~$0.654/mm² vs assumed TSMC N2 wafer ~$0.424/mm² and N3 ~$0.283/mm² (nominal wafer-area math).
Assumption ~$1.50/Gb DRAM; DRAMeXchange Sep 21 session-average 16Gb DDR5 eTT $24.80 → ~$1.55/Gb, implying ~$0.676/mm² for 1b density.
Caveat: N2/N3 figures are estimated foundry wafer prices; DRAM figures are selling value of bits — not fab cost — and ignore packaging/yield; TrendForce notes DDR5 spot deals remain thin.
stories.whyItMatters: AI memory scarcity is so extreme that memory makers can extract more revenue per square millimeter than cutting-edge logic wafers — with the usual apples-to-oranges caveats.
